title: Red Flags Before Marriage
audience: People in serious dating relationships considering marriage
speaker: Jonathan Noble
profession: Divorce and family law attorney (Pennsylvania and New Jersey)
core_message: Do not marry someone who cannot apologize sincerely or who shifts blame for their wrongdoing.

key_red_flags.name: No sincere apologies
key_red_flags.description: Your partner rarely or never gives a genuine apology for their mistakes.

key_red_flags.name: Keeping a suitcase of past mistakes
key_red_flags.description: Whenever you raise a concern, your partner brings up old issues from the past to deflect responsibility.

key_red_flags.name: Blame shifting
key_red_flags.description: Even when they do apologize, they justify their wrongdoing by blaming you for their actions.

examples: If you bring up a problem, your partner responds by listing your past mistakes instead of addressing the issue.
A partner saying: 'I cheated because you were out late,' instead of taking responsibility.
legal_warning: Jonathan warns that relationships with these traits often end up in divorce court.
main_content: As a divorce attorney, Jonathan Noble warns people about two major red flags before marriage. First, if your partner never gives a sincere apology and instead keeps a 'suitcase' of your past mistakes to use against you whenever you raise concerns, this is a dangerous sign. Second, if your partner engages in blame shifting — admitting wrongdoing but blaming you for causing it — this is another serious warning sign. According to Jonathan, these behaviors frequently lead to toxic relationships and divorce proceedings.
takeaway: If you notice habitual blame shifting or refusal to take responsibility, do not marry this person.
